statements.status_notes: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array; when subsequent partition additions reallocate the array, the pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. An attacker who can present a crafted block device image can trigger this without user interaction, since libblkid is invoked automatically by udev/udisks as root on block-device hot-plug events.
statements.impact_statement: This use-after-free in libblkid's nested partition probing (BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, UnixWare probers) is triggered automatically by udev/udisks as root on a block-device hot-plug event, such as a USB insertion or a loop-mounted disk image — containers do not perform hot-plug block-device management, and a source review of the Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no invocation of udev, udisks, blkid, or any partition-probing tool; the stock container's entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships bsdutils 1:2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.
